chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Muhammad ibn Marwan who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'What prevents one of you from being righteous with his parents, whether alive or dead? He can pray on their behalf, give charity on their behalf, perform Hajj on their behalf, and fast on their behalf. Thus, that which he does for them will be done for him, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will increase him, due to his righteousness and kinship, with much good.'

key_terms.يَبَرَّ: to be righteous / to do good to

ai.seo_question: How can a Muslim show righteousness to their parents after they have died?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that filial piety (birr) extends beyond the parents' lifetime through specific acts of worship—prayer, charity, Hajj, and fasting—performed on their behalf. This tradition highlights the Shia understanding of spiritual intercession for the deceased, where the son's continued devotion not only benefits the parents but also invites divine increase in his own goodness and kinship ties (silat al-rahim).
